A_target.statement:
Let $u, b: \closedint 0 T \to \R_{\ge 0}$ be [[Definition:Continuous Real Function|continuous]] and $a \ge 0$.
Suppose:
:$\displaystyle \map u t \le a + \int_0^t \map b s \map u s \rd s$
Then:
:$\displaystyle \map u t \le a \map \exp {\int_0^t \map b s \rd s}$

B_source.statement:
Let $u_n, b_n \ge 0$ and $a \ge 0$ satisfy:
:$\displaystyle u_n \le a + \sum_{k \mathop < n} b_k u_k$
Then:
:$\displaystyle u_n \le a \prod_{k \mathop < n} \paren {1 + b_k}$

substitutions.the index n: a time point t on a grid of spacing h
substitutions.the product of (1 + b_k): the exponential of the integral of b

derived.the limit of the discrete bound: the exponential bound a exp(int b)

validity_conditions: u must be nonnegative and continuous so the Riemann sums converge
b must be nonnegative and integrable for the product bound to converge to the exponential
the elementary bound 1 + x <= e^x is what makes the product-to-exponential passage one-directional
proof_plan:
Let $h = \dfrac T N$ and $t_k = k h$.
Replace the integral by its left [[Definition:Riemann Sum|Riemann sum]]:
:$\displaystyle \map u {t_n} \le a + \sum_{k \mathop < n} h \map b {t_k} \map u {t_k} + \epsilon_h$

By the discrete Gronwall inequality with $b_k = h \map b {t_k}$:
:$\displaystyle \map u {t_n} \le \paren {a + \epsilon_h} \prod_{k \mathop < n} \paren {1 + h \map b {t_k} }$

From [[Exponential of x not less than 1+x|$1 + x \le e^x$]]:
:$\displaystyle \prod_{k \mathop < n} \paren {1 + h \map b {t_k} } \le \map \exp {\sum_{k \mathop < n} h \map b {t_k} }$

Let $h \to 0$.
Then $\epsilon_h \to 0$ and the Riemann sum converges to $\displaystyle \int_0^t \map b s \rd s$.

Each step used only non-negativity and monotone bounds, so the inequality direction is preserved.
Hence:
:$\displaystyle \map u t \le a \map \exp {\int_0^t \map b s \rd s}$
{{qed}}
